title: Kestrel Networks to cut 9% of workforce as switch orders slip
author: Rafael Lindgren
text:
Kestrel Networks will cut 9% of its workforce, or about 380 jobs, as it trims costs after two hyperscale customers delayed orders for its data centre switches, the company said on Tuesday.

The layoffs fall mostly on sales and general administrative teams, while engineering roles tied to its new 800G products will be largely spared, according to an internal memo seen by Datacenter Dispatch.

Kestrel said it expects to record restructuring charges of $38 million to $45 million, mostly in the current period. The company kept its full-year outlook but said order timing would make results uneven.

"These are hard decisions affecting colleagues who helped build this company," said Gabriel Soto, Kestrel's president. "We are focusing our spending on the products customers are asking for."

The cuts come just over two weeks after Kestrel unveiled its Talon 8 switch, which it is counting on to win a larger share of AI cluster build-outs. Analysts said hyperscalers have been shifting purchases toward in-house designs, squeezing independent suppliers. Kestrel shares fell 6% in early trading.
